🔻 US miscalculated Iran’s resilience in war, Basij chief says

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Hossein Taeb, head of Iran’s Basij Organization, said the United States had accepted defeat in the military confrontation with Iran after miscalculating the country’s resilience and the ability of its armed forces to sustain the fight.

Speaking at a meeting in Tehran on Sunday, Taeb said the United States and Israel had expected Iran to capitulate within days or weeks, but the Iranian nation and Armed Forces had stood firm.
​
“They thought that if they could not achieve their objectives in three days, Iran’s resilience in the war would last no more than six weeks,” Taeb said.
​
He said the US and Israel had expected Iran to run short of ammunition and missiles, face economic disruption and experience domestic security pressures, forcing it to negotiate from a position of weakness.
​
“Those assessments proved wrong,” Taeb said, adding that the United States and Israel had also faced limitations in ammunition supplies and air defense capabilities, including dwindling stocks of THAAD interceptor missiles.
​
Taeb said Iran’s missile operations had become increasingly effective as the war progressed, with a growing proportion of missiles reaching their intended targets in Israeli-occupied territories.
​
He added that the United States and Israel had sought a ceasefire through European and regional intermediaries, expecting Iran to make concessions in subsequent negotiations.
​
Taeb said Washington and Tel Aviv were then forced to shift their strategy from direct, full-scale warfare toward proxy forces, regional and international alliances, and economic pressure after Iran gained full control over the Strait of Hormuz.
​
He described the conflict as a contest of endurance, stressing that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz had also imposed significant costs on the US and global economies.
​
Citing polls, Taeb said more than 70% of Americans believed the war with Iran had brought their country no meaningful benefits while imposing heavy costs. He also pointed to rising diesel prices and transportation costs as factors increasing the economic burden on American households, adding that European countries were beginning to experience the consequences as well.
​
Taeb called on Iranians to support the Armed Forces and strengthen the country’s deterrence capabilities, warning that any renewed aggression would be met with an unpredictable response.

🔻 Araghchi says Iran’s defense capabilities and diplomacy will safeguard national independence

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has stressed that Iran’s defense capabilities and diplomatic efforts will work toward safeguarding national independence, sovereignty and interests, emphasizing continued coordination between the foreign and defense ministries.

Araghchi made the remarks in a message on Sunday, congratulating Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi on his selection as minister of defense following a vote of confidence by the parliament.
​
The foreign minister expressed confidence that Akhlaghi’s technical expertise and managerial experience in Iran’s defense industries would help sustain the country’s progress and make more effective use of national capacities in fulfilling the ministry’s responsibilities.
​
Araghchi said defense capabilities and diplomacy, each within its respective area of responsibility, shared the common objective of protecting Iran’s independence, sovereignty and national interests.
​
He also reaffirmed the Foreign Ministry’s commitment to maintaining coordination and cooperation with the Ministry of Defense to safeguard Iran’s national interests and security.

💬 Russian foreign minister to visit Tehran on Monday: Iranian envoy

📌 Moscow, IRNA – Iranian Ambassador to Moscow, Kazem Jalali, has announced that Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov will visit Tehran on Monday as part of ongoing high-level consultations between the two countries.

In a post on his X account on Sunday, Jalali said that Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Russian President Vladimir Putin met last week in Awaza, Turkmenistan, marking their third meeting within a month.
​
He emphasized that, given the rapidly evolving developments, the close collaboration between Tehran and Moscow goes beyond their bilateral agenda, encompassing regional and international issues.
​
The ambassador added that the Iran-Russia partnership is grounded in both countries’ commitment to preserving and promoting peace, stability, and security in their surrounding regions, free from interference or disruption by external actors.

⚡️ IRGC chief pledges full support to new defense minister in countering enemy’s hybrid war

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The commander-in-chief of the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) has commended Mehrdad Akhlaqi on his appointment as Minister of Defense, after winning a vote of confidence in the parliament.

In a message on Sunday, Major General Ahmad Vahidi announced the IRGC's full readiness to foster strategic synergy and alignment with the Ministry of Defense, particularly in successfully countering the enemy’s hybrid war.
​
“I extend my sincere congratulations on your securing a decisive vote of confidence from the parliament and your appointment by President Masoud Pezeshkian as the Minister of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics,” he said in the message addressed to Akhlaqi.
​
He noted that the trust placed by the Parliament and the nation in the new defense minister reflects Akhlaqi’s commitment, capabilities, and proven competence to serve in this sensitive and vital position at critical times, in reference to constant enemy plots and military threats.
​
Major General Vahidi underscored the necessity of continuing the power-building and glorious path forged by Major General Aziz Nasirzadeh, the former minister of defense, who was assassinated in the US-Israeli attack.
​
At the end, the top IRGC commander wished Akhlaqi and all officials of the Ministry of Defense success, praying for their adherence to the enduring legacy of Imam Khomeini and the martyred Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, and for following the guidance of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei.
